item.title: Pitchamon Opatniputh Banned Three Months by BWF After Positive Doping Test
item.description: The 2023 world junior champion tested positive for furosemide ahead of the Asian Games in Nagoya, with her suspension backdated to expire on 20 December
item.content:encoded:
The Badminton World Federation (BWF) has handed Thailand's 19-year-old women's singles player Pitchamon Opatniputh a three-month suspension following an anti-doping rule violation, the governing body confirmed on Friday, 27 November 2026. Pitchamon tested positive for furosemide during an out-of-competition test conducted by the International Testing Agency (ITA) on 17 September 2026 in Nagoya, Japan, two days before the opening ceremony of the Asian Games.

The finding in Nagoya and the BWF ruling

Furosemide is prohibited at all times under section S5 of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) prohibited list as a diuretic and masking agent, substances that can facilitate rapid weight loss through fluid excretion or conceal the presence of other banned substances. Following the adverse analytical finding in her A-sample, Pitchamon requested the analysis of her B-sample, which was opened on 24 September 2026 in the presence of an independent witness and confirmed the presence of the substance. She accepted the violation under Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) rules, leading to her exclusion from the Asian Games and the withdrawal of her accreditation.

The BWF confirmed that her three-month sanction was backdated to begin from the date of her provisional suspension in September. "The matter has now concluded, with a three-month period of ineligibility commencing from her provisional suspension. Her period of ineligibility will expire on 20 December 2026," the BWF stated on its website. Thai sports minister Surasak Phancharoenworakul stated after the initial test that Pitchamon believed the substance originated from an anti-inflammatory ointment she had applied.

Ranking slide and immediate pathway back to the court

Pitchamon, who won the BWF World Junior Championships women's singles title in 2023, sat at world No. 18 when the provisional ban was imposed, though her absence from autumn tournaments has dropped her to No. 22. Prior to the sanction, she reached the final of the Indonesia Masters Super 500, losing to China's Chen Yufei, and finished as runner-up to Japan's Nozomi Okuhara at the Orleans Masters Super 300. Her senior titles on tour include the 2023 Malaysia Masters Super 100 and the 2025 Baoji China Masters Super 100.

Because the three-month period concludes on 20 December 2026, Pitchamon is cleared to return to competition on 21 December, leaving her eligible for the start of the 2027 BWF World Tour calendar in January. Neither Pitchamon nor the Badminton Association of Thailand issued an additional public response following Friday's BWF confirmation.

item.title: Musetti Stars in Singles and Doubles as Italy Edge Czech Republic to Reach Davis Cup Final
item.description: Lorenzo Musetti and Andrea Vavassori survived a deciding tiebreak in Bologna to send the three-time defending champions into their fourth straight final.
item.content:encoded:
Lorenzo Musetti delivered in both singles and doubles on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, to carry defending champions Italy past the Czech Republic 2-1 at the SuperTennis Arena in Bologna and into their fourth consecutive Davis Cup final.

Musetti anchors decisive doubles thriller

Musetti gave the host nation an opening advantage by defeating Jakub Mensik 6-3, 6-4 in the first singles rubber. Czech number one Jiri Lehecka responded immediately for the visitors, overcoming world No. 7 Flavio Cobolli 6-2, 1-6, 6-3 to square the semifinal tie and force a winner-take-all doubles contest.

Italian captain Filippo Volandri altered his doubles pairing from Wednesday's quarterfinal victory over South Korea, inserting Musetti alongside specialist Andrea Vavassori in place of Matteo Berrettini. Lehecka returned to the indoor hardcourt to partner Tomas Machac for Czechia, breaking Vavassori's serve early to claim the opening set 6-3.

The Italians struck back quickly in the second set, claiming two breaks of serve to wrap up a 6-1 set in under 30 minutes. The deciding set produced no breaks, though the Czech pair reached double break point at 4-3 on Vavassori's serve. Italy held serve, sent the contest into a final-set tiebreak, and clinched a 3-6, 6-1, 7-6 (7-4) victory after nearly two hours on court.

"This has a special meaning in my heart," Musetti said. "My last matches in Davis Cup weren't a win, so I felt like I needed this, to come back and prove that I could help the team. I don't have a voice because I screamed all the match, but I'm really happy and proud of what we did."

Chasing a fourth consecutive crown

The triumph stretched Italy's winning streak to 16 consecutive Davis Cup ties since September 2023. The Italians reached Sunday's championship tie without world No. 2 Jannik Sinner, who was ruled out of the Finals following right knee surgery. Czechia departed after beating Canada 2-0 in Tuesday's quarterfinals, falling just short of reaching their first final since 2013.

Sunday's final in Bologna pits Italy against the winner of Saturday's semifinal between Spain and Great Britain. If Italy lift the trophy on Sunday, Nov. 29, they will become the first nation to win four consecutive Davis Cup titles since the United States won five straight between 1968 and 1972.

item.title: Sotto and Debutant Boatwright Dominate as Gilas Pilipinas Rout Syria 97-58
item.description: A 39-point victory in Malaysia lifts the Philippines to 5-4 in FIBA World Cup qualifying ahead of a pivotal clash with Iran.
item.content:encoded:
Gilas Pilipinas recorded a 97-58 victory over Syria on Friday, 27 November 2026, at the Karisma Arena in Seremban, Malaysia, to open the fifth window of the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 Asian Qualifiers. The 39-point margin gave the Philippines their third consecutive win in Group E and lifted their overall qualifying record to 5-4.

Naturalized power forward Bennie Boatwright collected 16 points and 13 rebounds in his national team debut, partnering center Kai Sotto in the frontcourt. Sotto posted 18 points and 10 rebounds in 17 minutes and 40 seconds on the court. Head coach Tim Cone commended Boatwright's fast adjustment, stating, "We only had a few practices with Bennie Boatwright, and yet, he's fitting into us like a glove. He didn't go out and force anything, and stayed in what we do".

Record shooting breaks the deadlock

After an 18-18 tie in the opening quarter, the Philippines built a 43-32 advantage by halftime behind a 21-6 scoring run. Kevin Quiambao scored 18 points off the bench, converting six three-pointers on eight attempts to set a single-game record for a Philippine player in the qualifiers. Gilas outscored Syria 29-13 in the third quarter and 25-13 in the fourth, extending the advantage to a peak of 40 points at 95-55. Juan Gomez de Liaño added 11 points, while CJ Perez and Mike Phillips contributed 10 points apiece.

Glass control and defensive clamps

The Philippines controlled the interior, finishing with a 60-30 rebounding advantage and outscoring Syria 42-26 inside the paint. Gilas made 14 of 28 attempts from beyond the arc (50 percent) while limiting Syria to 30.6 percent shooting from the floor. Syrian naturalized guard D'Angelo Harrison scored 10 points on 3-of-15 shooting, while Mohamad Bilal Atli led the Syrian offense with 12 points and nine rebounds. The loss dropped Syria to 2-7, eliminating them from World Cup contention.

Group E standings tighten

The victory pulled the Philippines into a three-way tie for third place in Group E alongside Jordan and Iran at 5-4. Earlier on Friday, undefeated Australia clinched their spot at the 2027 World Cup at 9-0 by beating Iran 84-67, while New Zealand defeated Jordan 103-64 to improve to 7-2. Gilas face Iran on Sunday, 29 November, at the Karisma Arena before concluding the qualifying tournament on home soil in Cebu City in February 2027.

item.title: United States and West Indies Lined Up as Preferred Co-Hosts for 2034 Men's T20 World Cup
item.description: The ICC has set the 2034 tournament for July and August, and a joint North American and Caribbean event is the preferred option, according to The Guardian.
item.content:encoded:
The United States and the West Indies are being lined up to co-host the 2034 men's T20 World Cup, The Guardian reported, ten years after the two shared the 2024 tournament. The decision is not final: the International Cricket Council still lists the 2034 hosts as "to be confirmed".

At its board meetings in Bali from 11 to 15 November 2026, the ICC approved the windows for its events up to 2035. The 2034 men's T20 World Cup is set for 6 July to 6 August, a northern-summer slot that, according to The Guardian, rules out venues in Asia, Africa and Oceania. England, Ireland and Scotland will host the 2030 edition in the same part of the year, and the England and Wales Cricket Board is understood not to be bidding for 2034, the newspaper reported. That leaves a joint North American and Caribbean event as the preferred option.

Bigger plans for the US

The United States is seen as especially important to the ICC, partly because cricket will be played at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, The Guardian reported. At the 2024 World Cup, the US staged 16 matches at three venues, in Grand Prairie (Texas), Lauderhill (Florida) and a temporary stadium in Nassau County, New York, while the West Indies hosted the other 39.

For 2034, the venues being discussed include the temporary Olympic cricket ground in Pomona, California, Frederick near Washington DC, the Oakland Coliseum and Marymoor Park in Seattle, as well as the 2024 grounds in Texas and Florida, according to The Guardian.

The two boards are already working together. West Indies are set to host India for two T20 internationals in North America in July 2027, with Washington DC and Toronto among the front-runners to stage them, ESPN reported.

USA Cricket's problems first

Any award depends on USA Cricket sorting out its governance. The ICC has suspended the national body, ESPNcricinfo reported, and USA Cricket filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in 2025. According to The Guardian, the ICC has lent it money to keep staff working, and the owners of Major League Cricket have put up $3 million (£2.3 million) for a rescue plan, which is expected to be settled next year.

The ICC plans to finalise how it awards future tournaments in 2027, and hosting rights for events after 2031 are likely to be handed out from 2028.

item.title: Alexander Ovechkin: The Moscow Prodigy Who Broke Wayne Gretzky's NHL Record
item.description: From a childhood loss in Moscow to the NHL goals record and a farewell season: the story of the Washington Capitals captain.
item.content:encoded:
On 6 April 2025, at UBS Arena in Elmont, New York, Alexander Ovechkin scored a second-period power-play goal past New York Islanders goaltender Ilya Sorokin. It was the 895th regular-season goal of his NHL career and broke Wayne Gretzky's record of 894, which had stood since Gretzky retired in 1999. After the game, Gretzky shook his hand during an on-ice ceremony for the 39-year-old Washington Capitals captain. Sorokin was the 183rd different goaltender Ovechkin had scored against, ESPN reported.

A sporting family in Moscow

Ovechkin was born on 17 September 1985 in Moscow. His mother, Tatyana Ovechkina, won Olympic gold with the Soviet basketball team in 1976 and 1980, and his father, Mikhail, played football for Dynamo Moscow. He picked up a hockey stick at the age of two and later joined the Dynamo Moscow youth academy.

His older brother Sergei often took him to training. When Ovechkin was 10, Sergei, then in his early twenties, died of a blood clot after a car accident, Sports Illustrated reported.

As a boy in the Dynamo system, Ovechkin scored 56 goals in one season, beating the club academy record of 53 held by Pavel Bure, according to Wikipedia.

From Dynamo to Washington

Ovechkin made his senior debut for Dynamo Moscow in the Russian Superleague in 2001–02, aged 16. In four seasons he scored 36 goals and added 32 assists in 152 games, and helped Dynamo win the 2004–05 Russian title. A year earlier, in 2004, the Washington Capitals had made him the first overall pick in the NHL Draft.

After the 2004–05 NHL season was cancelled by a lockout, Ovechkin made his NHL debut on 5 October 2005 and scored twice against the Columbus Blue Jackets in a 3–2 win. On 16 January 2006 against the Phoenix Coyotes, he was knocked to the ice by Paul Mara and, while sliding on his back, hooked the puck past goaltender Brian Boucher with one hand, a goal commentators still call "The Goal". He finished his rookie season with 52 goals and 54 assists and won the Calder Trophy as the league's best rookie.

Trophies and the Stanley Cup

Washington named Ovechkin captain on 5 January 2010. He won the Hart Trophy as league MVP in 2008, 2009 and 2013, the players' award for the most outstanding player three years in a row from 2008 to 2010 (the Lester B. Pearson Award, renamed the Ted Lindsay Award in 2010), and the Maurice "Rocket" Richard Trophy as the top goal scorer nine times. With Russia he won the World Championship in 2008, 2012 and 2014.

His long wait for a title ended on 7 June 2018 at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, when the Capitals beat the Vegas Golden Knights 4–3 in Game 5 to win the franchise's first Stanley Cup. Ovechkin scored 15 goals in the playoffs and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP.

The record and the last season

In 2024–25 he missed 16 games with a fractured left fibula and still scored 44 goals in 65 games, including the record-breaking 895th, which also made him the NHL's all-time leader in power-play goals. On 22 March 2026 against Colorado he scored his 1,000th NHL goal including the playoffs, NHL.com reported, a milestone previously reached only by Gretzky.

On 5 October 2026, 21 years to the day after his NHL debut, Ovechkin announced that the 2026–27 season would be his last in the NHL. He began it with 929 regular-season goals, according to NHL.com, and remains Washington's captain in his farewell season.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Beat China 82-80 in FIBA World Cup Qualifiers for First Win in 33 Years
item.description: A 16.7 percent shooting night from deep and Zhou Qi's ejection leave China at 5-4 in Group F.
item.content:encoded:
Saudi Arabia defeated China 82-80 on Thursday, November 26, in the fifth window of the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 Asian Qualifiers at Al Janoub Arena in Doha, Qatar. It was Saudi Arabia's first win over China in a major FIBA competition since the 1993 Asia Cup, FIBA reported; Saudi Arabia had lost the previous six meetings.

Zhou Qi ejection shifts momentum

China opened the game with a 10-2 run and led 29-25 after the first quarter. Saudi Arabia answered in the second period, outscoring China 23-14 to take a 48-43 advantage into halftime.

A pivotal moment occurred with 4:44 remaining in the third quarter when China center Zhou Qi was assessed a disqualifying foul for an elbow during interior positioning. Zhou was ejected after scoring 10 points on 5-of-6 shooting in 11 minutes. Saudi Arabia pushed the lead to eight before China trimmed the deficit to 68-66 at the end of the third quarter. Early in the fourth, guard Liao Sanning led a China comeback, and forward Li Hongquan made three free throws to give China a 75-72 lead in the closing minutes.

Shooting woes prove decisive

Saudi Arabia regained control during the final minutes. Forward Ali Shubayli sank two free throws with six seconds left to give Saudi Arabia an 82-79 lead. Hu made the first of two free throws with two seconds remaining, secured his own rebound after intentionally missing the second, but his buzzer-beating three-point attempt bounced off the rim.

China converted just 5 of 30 attempts from three-point range (16.7 percent), while Saudi Arabia went 7-for-23. The poor shooting cancelled out China's work on the boards, where they collected 25 offensive rebounds.

Saudi center Mohammad Alsuwailem led all scorers with 20 points, four assists and two blocks. Four other Saudi players reached double figures: Khaled Gabar with 15 points, Marzouq Almuwallad with 13, and Shubayli and Mohammad-Ali Abdur-Rahkman with 12 each. Liao and Hu led China with 15 points apiece, while Hu Jinqiu added 14 points and seven rebounds.

Complications in Group F

"Poor three-point shooting was the key to our defeat," China head coach Guo Shiqiang said, according to Xinhua. "We lost an important game and now we will face a more difficult task in securing World Cup qualification."

The loss dropped China to a 5-4 record in Group F, tied with South Korea, who hold the head-to-head tiebreaker after two earlier victories over China. Saudi Arabia moved to 4-5 to remain in contention for qualification. China next plays an away fixture against Lebanon on November 29.

item.title: Dortmund Lead Bundesliga by Two Points as Kane Injury Leaves Bayern Short
item.description: Niko Kovač's unbeaten side top the table after ten games, while Vincent Kompany's Bayern lost their first match of the season at Lille without Harry Kane.
item.content:encoded:
Borussia Dortmund lead the Bundesliga by two points after ten rounds. Niko Kovač's side have 24 points from seven wins and three draws, ahead of Bayern Munich and Freiburg on 22, according to the official Bundesliga table. Neither Dortmund nor Bayern has lost a league game this season.

Dortmund's last German title came in 2012 under Jürgen Klopp. In 2023 they lost the title on the final day after a 2-2 draw with Mainz, when Bayern finished level on points and won on goal difference.

Built on defence

Dortmund's lead rests on their defence. They have conceded only seven goals in ten games, the Bundesliga table shows. Bayern have scored far more, 30 goals to Dortmund's 17, but have dropped points in four draws.

Kovač is also missing players. Giannis Konstantelias tore the cruciate ligament in his left knee on his debut against Hamburg on 29 August, and the club said he would be out for several months. Captain Emre Can has not played since tearing his cruciate ligament against Bayern on 28 February.

Bayern without Kane

Bayern's problems have grown in the last week. Harry Kane injured ligaments in his left ankle in the 1-1 draw with Köln on 20 November and had surgery. The club said he would be out "for the next few months", and sporting director Max Eberl spoke of about three months, ESPN reported. Kane has scored 156 goals in 161 games for Bayern, according to Al Jazeera.

Five days later Bayern lost 2-1 at Lille in the Champions League, their first defeat of the season, AP reported. Dayot Upamecano scored for Bayern.

Vincent Kompany's injury list is long. Goalkeeper Manuel Neuer is out, Michael Olise has a bruised forefoot and will miss Saturday's trip to Hamburg, Serge Gnabry and Alphonso Davies have hamstring injuries, and Ismael Saibari has had ankle surgery, according to AP and ESPN. There is better news on Luis Díaz, who returned as a substitute at Lille, and Jamal Musiala, who has come off the bench in the last two matches.

The weekend ahead

Bayern play at Hamburger SV on Saturday, 28 November. Dortmund host Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday, 29 November. Leverkusen know what an unbeaten title run looks like: in 2023-24 they went through the Bundesliga season without a defeat and finished 17 points clear.

item.title: Marc Marquez Announces MotoGP Retirement Days After Winning Record-Equalling Eighth Title
item.description: The 33-year-old Spaniard will race for the last time at this weekend's Valencia Grand Prix, level with Giacomo Agostini on eight premier-class titles.
item.content:encoded:
Eight-time MotoGP world champion Marc Marquez announced his retirement on Friday, 27 November 2026, at the Circuit Ricardo Tormo in Valencia, Spain. This weekend's Valencia Grand Prix, the last round of the season, will be the final race of his career.

Cards in the Ducati garage

Marquez broke the news in the Ducati Lenovo Team garage at the start of the first practice session, holding up handwritten cards to the live television cameras. The first card read "We'll talk later but first", Crash.net reported. The cards went on to say "This will be my last race in MotoGP" and "We made history", according to AP.

"It is official. Marc Marquez has decided to retire from MotoGP," Ducati said. MotoGP called him a rider who "bows out on top as reigning Champion".

At a press conference at the circuit later on Friday, the 33-year-old explained his choice. "I arrived in MotoGP in my way, and I will go in my way," he said, as quoted by Crash.net. He added that "the situation this year was very in the limit". According to Crash.net, he made the decision after the Japanese Grand Prix at Motegi in October, and only his brother Alex knew.

A title won from 102 points behind

Marquez clinched the 2026 championship five days earlier at the Portuguese Grand Prix in Portimão on 22 November, where eighth place was enough. The title drew him level with Giacomo Agostini's record of eight premier-class crowns and moved him one ahead of Valentino Rossi. Counting his 125cc title in 2010 and his Moto2 title in 2012, it was his tenth world championship, Anadolu Agency reported.

The season began badly. Marquez fell 102 points behind Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi, a deficit that AP and MCNews describe as the largest ever overturned in MotoGP. He has won seven Grands Prix and ten Sprint races this season and took the title with a round to spare.

Injuries behind the decision

The announcement surprised the paddock because Marquez signed a contract extension in June 2026 covering 2027 and 2028, the first seasons of the new 850cc rules. His career was shaped by injuries: he broke his right humerus at Jerez in 2020 and needed four operations, according to MotoGP, and he also needed surgery on his right shoulder after Bezzecchi collided with him on the first lap of the Indonesian Grand Prix, Motorsport.com reported.

MotoGP said the Valencia weekend will celebrate his career under the hashtag #ThankYouMarc.

item.title: Svay Rieng Stun Machida as Crown Fall in Kuching: ACL Two Matchday 5 Round-Up
item.description: Svay Rieng beat Japan's Machida Zelvia 2-0 in Phnom Penh, Phnom Penh Crown lost 3-0 in Malaysia, and both Cambodian clubs still lead their own fate into the final round
item.content:encoded:
Cambodian football had its best and toughest nights in Asia within a few hours of each other on Thursday, 26 November. In Phnom Penh, Preah Khan Reach Svay Rieng beat Japan's FC Machida Zelvia 2-0, handing the Group G leaders their first defeat of the AFC Champions League Two. In Malaysia, Phnom Penh Crown lost 3-0 to Kuching City, but stayed top of Group H.

After five of six group matches, both Cambodian clubs know a draw in the final round on 3 December will take them into the Round of 16. Here is how Matchday 5 went in all eight groups, and what each team said about it.

Svay Rieng 2-0 Machida Zelvia: Cambodia's night of the season

Svay Rieng played the match at Morodok Techo National Stadium. Machida arrived having won all four group games, including a 2-0 win over Svay Rieng in Japan on the first matchday.

The first half was even. Kwame Peprah shot just wide early on, and goalkeeper Vireak Dara made a fine left-handed save from Takahiro Akimoto in the 24th minute, the AFC reported. Tiago Alves had the best chance of the half when he was sent through on goal, but he pulled his shot wide.

Machida changed two players at half-time, but Svay Rieng scored first. In the 59th minute, Alessandro Martins Júnior curled a low shot past goalkeeper Kosei Tani from the edge of the box. Thirteen minutes later, Rui Pires lifted the ball over Machida's defence, Alves beat the offside trap and chipped the ball over Tani for 2-0.

Machida pushed for a way back. Futa Tokumura's long shot hit the crossbar and Kim Min-tae's header hit the post, according to the AFC. Dara and his defence kept a clean sheet to the end.

What worked for Svay Rieng: they kept their shape against a side that had more of the ball (ESPN's statistics gave Machida 56% possession) and took their chances in a 13-minute spell after the break. Coach Matthew McConkey said a small tactical change made the difference. "We wanted to encourage the opponents to press us, because when they pushed forward, spaces would open up behind them for us to attack," he told the Phnom Penh Post. "We performed well, and this is the level our club demonstrated in this match." Kampuchea Thmey called it the first win by a Cambodian club over a Japanese club, a week after Svay Rieng beat Thailand's Port FC 4-1 in the ASEAN Club Championship.

What went wrong for Machida: it was their first defeat in the tournament, and, according to Soccer Digest, their first in 15 competitive matches. Coach Go Kuroda said his team had little time to prepare after finishing their J1 League season just before the trip, the Phnom Penh Post reported; he also mentioned the heat in Phnom Penh, according to Kampuchea Thmey. But he did not hide behind it. "I knew Svay Rieng would play on the counterattack in this match, and we prepared for that, but our players still did not perform well enough," Kuroda said.

Svay Rieng now have 10 points, two behind Machida, who are already through. Their last game is away to Shanghai Shenhua on 3 December. Shenhua have 7 points and must win; a draw is enough for Svay Rieng, Troryorng reported. The first meeting between the two sides in Cambodia ended 0-0.

Kuching City 3-0 Phnom Penh Crown: punished on the break

In Kuching, the home side started fast. Ajdin Mujagić headed against the post in the opening minutes and had a goal ruled out for offside, Utusan Sarawak reported. Safawi Rasid gave Kuching the lead in the 32nd minute. Before half-time, Kuching goalkeeper Haziq Nadzli made a strong save to keep Crown from equalising.

Crown improved after the break and pushed forward, but were caught on the counter. Jerome Mpacko Etame scored within a minute of coming on for Safawi in the 75th minute, and Dylan Wenzel-Halls added a third in stoppage time.

What went wrong for Crown: coach Oleg Starynskyi felt the score was harsher than the game. "It was a tough result because we didn't deserve to lose 3-0," he told the AFC. "They punished us with a counterattack, and that second goal made things difficult," he said, as quoted by Utusan Sarawak (translated from Malay). He added: "The group is very tough."

What worked for Kuching: coach Aidil Sharin Sahak praised his players' discipline and effort, and said the result made up for their 2-1 defeat in Phnom Penh earlier in the group. "We didn't deserve to lose in Phnom Penh," he told the AFC, adding that "the team is really growing". Safawi, named man of the match, said the win "isn't just for me, but for the entire team" (translated from Malay, Utusan Sarawak).

On the same night, Gangwon FC beat Kitchee 3-2 in Gangneung. Kitchee led twice, through Everton Camargo in the first minute and Asier Illarramendi early in the second half. Kim Dae-won scored twice for Gangwon, and Shin Min-ha headed the winner from Kim's cross in stoppage time, the AFC reported.

Group H now reads: Phnom Penh Crown 9 points, Kuching City 7, Gangwon 7, Kitchee 5. On 3 December, Crown host Gangwon and Kuching visit Kitchee. On these numbers, a draw would be enough for Crown to go through. A defeat would put them out only if Kuching also beat Kitchee.

Around the East

Group E: Persib Bandung beat FC Seoul 3-1 in Bandung to make it five wins out of five and finish top. Seoul, the Korean champions, rotated their squad, levelled through Leonardo Ruiz but conceded again before half-time and lost Moon Seon-min to a red card in the 70th minute, the AFC reported. "Good defence, good transitions, three goals," said Persib coach Igor Tolic (translated from Indonesian, Antara). Seoul coach Kim Gi-dong said he wanted to apologise to the supporters (translated, JPNN). In Geelong, Melbourne Victory and The Cong-Viettel drew 0-0. Victory missed several good chances, and coach Giovanni Savarese said his team needed to be more "killers" in front of goal. The draw put Viettel out. Persib have 15 points, Seoul 6, Victory 5 and Viettel 2. Seoul host Victory on 2 December.

Group F: Singapore's Lion City Sailors won 3-0 away to BG Pathum United, with goals from Ilhan Fandi, Hugo Gomes and Matthias Phaëton, to win the group with a game to spare. "It was a collective performance throughout the game," said coach Mark Jackson. Pathum coach Peerapong Pichitchotirat admitted: "We have to accept that we weren't the better team today." Adelaide United won 7-1 away to Tai Po in Hong Kong, with four goals from 20-year-old Burkitt; Tai Po had Paulinho sent off. Adelaide coach Airton Andrioli kept calm: "We've achieved nothing at the moment." The Sailors have 13 points, Adelaide 9 and Pathum 7. Adelaide host Pathum in the final round.

Group G: Shanghai Shenhua beat Tampines Rovers 7-1 in Singapore. Xie Pengfei scored a hat-trick, Rafael Ratão and Luis Asué two each. Tampines scored through Seiga Sumi but had Amirul Haikal sent off early in the second half for a foul in the box; Shenhua's Wilson Manafa hit the crossbar with the penalty. The result keeps Shenhua's hopes alive for their final-round meeting with Svay Rieng.

Around the West

Group A: Al Wahda came from behind to win 2-1 at Kuwait SC and are through as group winners on 12 points. Kuwait led through Ibrahim Kamil, but Wahda scored twice in the last half hour. "We will fight until the very end," said coach Péricles Chamusca. Nasaf beat Al Khaldiya 1-0 in Qarshi through an Abbosjon Gulomov goal early in the second half, which put Khaldiya out. Nasaf coach Ruziqul Berdiyev complained that "VAR is not working in the tournament" after a late incident (zamin.uz). Nasaf (7) visit Wahda on 9 December; Kuwait (6) need to win and hope Nasaf do not.

Group B: Al Jazira beat Gol Gohar 1-0 with a 40th-minute shot from Anderson Talisca and are through on 13 points. Turkmenistan's Arkadag joined them by winning 4-2 at Al Muharraq, who had Bruno Santos sent off in the third minute and played almost the whole match with ten men. Dayanc Meredow scored twice. Arkadag (10) host Jazira for first place.

Group C: Aleksandar Mitrović volleyed in after the Al Faisaly goalkeeper spilled a shot, giving Al Rayyan a 1-0 win in Amman. Al Taawoun, who rested several key players, were held 0-0 at home by Al Nahda; Abderrazak Hamdallah came off the bench and hit the woodwork. Rayyan (12) and Taawoun (11) are both through and meet to decide first place.

Group D: East Bengal beat Jordan's Al Hussein 1-0 in Kolkata with an 87th-minute goal from a corner by Jeakson Singh, the first ACL Two win by an Indian club, according to Khel Now and The Open Press. item.title: Italy Beat South Korea 2-1 to Reach Davis Cup Semifinals
item.description: Matteo Berrettini and Andrea Vavassori won the deciding doubles after world No. 139 Soonwoo Kwon beat Flavio Cobolli.
item.content:encoded:
Three-time defending champion Italy held off South Korea on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, winning 2-1 at BolognaFiere in Bologna to reach the Davis Cup semifinals. Matteo Berrettini and Andrea Vavassori won the deciding doubles rubber against Soonwoo Kwon and Hyeon Chung 7-6 (7-2), 7-6 (13-11), saving four set points in the second set.

Kwon beats French Open finalist Cobolli

Lorenzo Musetti gave the hosts a 1-0 lead. The world No. 27 beat Hong Seong-chan, ranked 787th, 6-0, 7-6 (7-5) in just over 90 minutes, the Korea Herald reported.

South Korea drew level through Kwon, ranked 139th. He came from a set down to beat world No. 7 and 2026 French Open runner-up Flavio Cobolli 3-6, 7-6 (7-3), 7-6 (7-5) in two hours and 50 minutes. Kwon trailed 3-1 in the final tiebreak before winning six of the last eight points.

"He played an unbelievable match from the second set," Cobolli said, according to Tennis Majors. "There is no ranking here, there are only two teams that fight for the same goal."

Doubles decides the tie

Kwon was back on court about 20 minutes after his singles win, partnering Chung, a semifinalist at the 2018 Australian Open. Both teams held serve throughout the first set, and Berrettini and Vavassori took the tiebreak 7-2.

The second set also went to a tiebreak. South Korea had four set points, but the Italians saved all of them and, after the tiebreak reached 11-11, converted their third match point to win 13-11 after one hour and 54 minutes.

"I didn't feel any pressure. I think I really enjoyed playing for the first time in a while," Kwon said afterwards, JKN reported.

Italy's run reaches 15 ties

The win extended Italy's unbeaten run in Davis Cup ties to 15. Captain Filippo Volandri's team play Czechia in the semifinals on Friday, 27 November 2026. Czechia beat Canada 2-0 on Tuesday, the ATP reported.

It was South Korea's first Davis Cup quarterfinal, 66 years after the country first entered the competition in 1960. The South Korean team had no player ranked inside the top 100 in singles or doubles, yet took the hosts to five tiebreaks across the three rubbers.

item.title: From a Paper Napkin to 47 Trophies: The Life and Legacy of Lionel Messi
item.description: Overcoming growth hormone deficiency in Rosario, the Argentine maestro built football's most decorated career across Barcelona, Paris, and Miami.
item.content:encoded:
No player in the professional game has won more than Lionel Andrés Messi: 47 senior team trophies from more than 1,150 career appearances. Over a senior career spanning more than two decades, the Argentine forward has scored over 930 goals and delivered more than 420 assists for club and country, earning eight Ballons d'Or, six European Golden Shoes, and eight FIFA world player awards.

Messi was born in Rosario, in Santa Fe Province, on 24 June 1987, and grew up in the working-class Las Heras district. His father, Jorge Messi, worked as a department head at an Acindar pressed steel plant in nearby Villa Constitución, while his mother, Celia Cuccittini, had a job in a workshop that made magnets. Messi was the third of four children, alongside his older brothers Rodrigo and Matías and his younger sister María Sol. Two of his cousins in Rosario, Maximiliano and Emanuel Biancucchi, also went on to play the game professionally.

Messi started kicking a ball at the age of four with local club Abanderado Grandoli, where his father served as coach. His maternal grandmother, Celia, regularly accompanied him to pitches across the neighbourhood and pushed coaches to give the diminutive boy playing time. Her death shortly before his eleventh birthday left an indelible mark on him. Messi has marked virtually every goal of his career by pointing both index fingers toward the sky in her memory.

The Rosario Crucible and the Barcelona Napkin

At age seven, Messi joined Newell's Old Boys, the Rosario club he has supported throughout his life. Over six seasons with Newell's, he scored nearly 500 goals as a member of "The Machine of '87," a youth squad named after their birth year that dominated youth circuits across the region. During half-time breaks of Newell's senior matches, Messi regularly juggled the ball on the pitch to entertain home supporters, idolising Brazilian striker Ronaldo and River Plate playmaker Pablo Aimar.

Crisis struck when Messi was 10 years old. Doctors diagnosed him with a growth hormone deficiency, a condition requiring daily subcutaneous injections that cost at least 1,000 Argentine pesos per month. Jorge Messi's workplace health insurance covered only two years of treatment, and Newell's reneged on an agreement to fund the remainder. River Plate offered to sign him after a four-goal trial and pay for his hormone therapy, but Newell's refused to release his registration card.

Faced with mounting medical costs, the family turned to relatives in Catalonia to arrange a trial with FC Barcelona in September 2000, when Messi was 13. Barcelona first-team director Carles Rexach was captivated by his trial matches, but the board hesitated to commit money to a foreign boy so young. On 14 December 2000, an ultimatum from Messi's camp led Rexach to draft an agreement on a paper napkin, pledging Barcelona's commitment.

In February 2001, the Messi family moved into an apartment near Camp Nou. The transition proved painful. Transfer paperwork disputes with Newell's restricted Messi to friendlies and Catalan league fixtures during his first year. In the dressing room, he spoke so quietly that teammates initially wondered if he was mute. Homesickness fractured the household; his mother and siblings returned to Rosario, leaving Messi alone in Barcelona with his father.

La Masia, Trophies, and Heartbreak in Blue and White

By February 2002, the Royal Spanish Football Federation cleared Messi for full competition. At 14, he completed his growth hormone therapy and took his place in Barcelona's "Baby Dream Team" alongside Cesc Fàbregas and Gerard Piqué. During the 2002–03 campaign, he scored 36 goals in 30 games for Cadetes A. In the Copa Catalunya final against Espanyol, played a week after suffering a fractured cheekbone, he discarded a protective plastic mask after several minutes of discomfort and scored two goals inside 10 minutes to seal a 4–1 win.

Messi made his La Liga debut for Barcelona on 16 October 2004, aged 17. Over the next 17 seasons he collected 34 trophies, a club record, among them 10 league titles and four Champions League crowns. He scored 672 goals for Barcelona, establishing an all-time record for a single club. In the 2008–09 season, under Pep Guardiola, he led Barcelona to the first treble in Spanish football history. Six years later, alongside Luis Suárez and Neymar in the "MSN" frontline, he captured a historic second European treble in 2014–15.

International success arrived at a far slower pace. After capturing Olympic gold at Beijing 2008, Messi assumed the Argentina captaincy in 2011. He carried his country to three consecutive major finals—the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, the 2015 Copa América in Chile, and the 2016 Copa América Centenario in the United States—all of which ended in extra-time or penalty-shootout defeats. Devastated, Messi announced his international retirement in June 2016 before changing his mind soon afterwards.

Final Glories from Lusail to South Florida

Financial mismanagement at Barcelona brought an abrupt end to Messi's stay in Catalonia in August 2021. He joined Paris Saint-Germain as a free agent and won two Ligue 1 titles there. Concurrently, his national team fortunes reversed. Messi captained Argentina to the 2021 Copa América title at the Maracanã, their first major trophy in 28 years. At the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, Messi scored seven goals and led Argentina past France in a dramatic final at Lusail Stadium, capturing the trophy that had eluded him.

In July 2023, Messi signed with Major League Soccer club Inter Miami, transforming the sport's profile across North America. He led Miami to the 2023 Leagues Cup, the club's first trophy, and was named MLS MVP in 2024 and 2025. With Argentina he won the Copa América again in 2024.

After the 2026 World Cup, where Argentina lost the final to Spain on 19 July, Messi announced his retirement from international football on 31 August 2026, ESPN reported. He returned for one farewell match against Benin at the Monumental on 6 October 2026, scoring a penalty and setting up two goals in a 3-0 win, according to AP. He finished his Argentina career with 208 caps and 126 goals.

item.title: Daniel Dubois to Defend WBO Heavyweight Title Against Joseph Parker in Manchester
item.description: The heavyweight showdown at Co-op Live on 30 January 2027 settles unfinished business after their cancelled 2025 clash.
item.content:encoded:
Daniel Dubois will make the second defence of his WBO heavyweight world title against former champion Joseph Parker at Manchester's Co-op Live arena on Saturday, 30 January 2027. Promoter Frank Warren and Queensberry Promotions officially announced the bout, billed as "New Year's Retribution", on 25 November 2026, with DAZN securing live broadcast coverage.

Dubois, 29, enters the contest with a record of 24 victories and three defeats, having stopped 23 opponents inside the distance. The London heavyweight claimed the WBO belt in May 2026 with an 11th-round technical knockout of Fabio Wardley at the same Manchester arena, before halting Wardley in two rounds in an immediate London rematch on 17 October. Dubois previously held the IBF world title, which he defended in September 2024 by knocking out Anthony Joshua in front of 96,000 spectators at Wembley Stadium.

Unfinished business from Riyadh

The January clash resurrects a contest originally scheduled for February 2025 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where Dubois was slated to face Parker. Dubois withdrew during fight week due to illness, leaving Parker to face late substitute Martin Bakole, whom the New Zealander stopped in the second round.

Dubois subsequently vacated his interim belt before regaining world championship status against Wardley. "Daniel is entering his prime and when he is on his game it is hard to picture anybody beating him," Warren said in Queensberry's official fight announcement. "But Joseph has long promised to become world champion again, and now he gets his chance."

Parker's path back to a belt

Parker, 34, carries a professional record of 36 wins and four defeats, with 24 knockouts. The Auckland-born heavyweight held the WBO belt between December 2016 and March 2018, losing the title on points to Joshua in Cardiff. Parker re-established himself in title contention with consecutive decisions over former champions Deontay Wilder and Zhilei Zhang between late 2023 and early 2024.

The challenger has not fought since October 2025, when he suffered a late stoppage loss against Wardley. Parker was handed a provisional anti-doping suspension following that bout, which was formally rescinded in August 2026.

The heavyweight landscape in 2027

The Manchester date opens the 2027 calendar for a division where unified champion Oleksandr Usyk and IBF titlist Filip Hrgovic hold the remaining belts. The winner at Co-op Live is positioned to enter unification negotiations later in the year, with Dubois pursuing undisputed status and Parker seeking a second WBO title reign nine years after his first championship victory.

item.title: Bennie Boatwright Debuts as Kai Sotto Boosts Gilas Pilipinas for FIBA Window 5
item.description: Tim Cone unveils a towering frontline in Malaysia as the Philippines targets crucial Group E wins against Syria and Iran.
item.content:encoded:
Gilas Pilipinas finalized its preparations on Thursday in Seremban, Malaysia, ahead of Friday's 2027 FIBA Basketball World Cup Asian Qualifiers meeting with Syria at Karisma Arena. Head coach Tim Cone will hand 6-foot-10 naturalized forward Bennie Boatwright his international debut, pairing him alongside 7-foot-3 center Kai Sotto in an expanded frontline for the penultimate qualifying window.

A towering frontline for Seremban

Sotto, the 24-year-old center playing for Altiri Chiba in Japan's B.League, averaged 15.5 points and 15.0 rebounds per game during the fourth window in August 2026, when the Philippines defeated Jordan and Iran at the Mall of Asia Arena. Sotto confirmed during an online press conference on Tuesday that he is cleared to play despite managing knee swelling from his club campaign.

"Ako gusto ko lagi may kasama akong malaki na makakasama ko sa court," Sotto told reporters, noting that Boatwright's outside shooting allows the frontline to stretch the floor without losing size. Gilas also features 6-foot-10 AJ Edu, 6-foot-9 Quentin Millora-Brown, and 6-foot-8 Mike Phillips, with Kevin Quiambao and Troy Rosario bolstering the forward rotation.

Crash course in Cone's triangle

Boatwright obtained his Philippine passport in October 2026, stepping into the naturalized player role following an injury to veteran Justin Brownlee. The 30-year-old former USC forward arrived in Seremban on November 22 after completing his stint with the Fujian Sturgeons in the Chinese Basketball Association. Gilas tested the combination on Tuesday, defeating Malaysian club KL Hornbills in a tune-up game.

"It's complicated," Boatwright said of Cone's triangle offense. "You have to know reads. It's not just a simple call and play... but my teammates are making it very easy on me." Former San Miguel teammate CJ Perez helped guide Boatwright through the sets alongside backcourt regulars Scottie Thompson, Dwight Ramos, Chris Newsome, and Juan Gomez de Liaño.

The qualification race in Group E

The Philippines enters Window 5 sitting fifth in Group E with a 4-4 record (12 points), chasing Australia (8-0), New Zealand (6-2), Iran (5-3), and Jordan (5-3), while Syria stands at 2-6. The top three teams in each group, alongside the best fourth-placed team across both Asian qualifying pools, qualify for the 2027 FIBA Basketball World Cup in Qatar.

"What happens on paper doesn't necessarily translate to the floor," Cone said. "That's why you have practice and you work with the guys on the floor." Gilas faces Syria on Friday, November 27, and meets Iran on Sunday, November 29, before closing the qualifying schedule on home soil in Cebu in February 2027.

item.title: On This Day in 1917: How an Owner Feud Birthed the National Hockey League
item.description: Frustrated by Toronto Blueshirts owner Eddie Livingstone, rival NHA executives met at Montreal's Windsor Hotel to create a breakaway competition.
item.content:encoded:
On November 26, 1917, representatives from four National Hockey Association clubs met at the Windsor Hotel in Montreal and signed an agreement to abandon their existing organisation and establish a new competition: the National Hockey League. The breakaway was not conceived as a grand continental blueprint, but as a legal loophole designed to freeze out Edward James Livingstone, the combative principal owner of the Toronto Blueshirts.

Four club figures gathered in the Montreal hotel room to formalise the split: Sam Lichtenhein of the Montreal Wanderers, George Kennedy of the Montreal Canadiens, Tommy Gorman on behalf of the Ottawa Senators, and Mike Quinn of the Quebec Bulldogs. Former NHA secretary Frank Calder was elected the NHL's first president. When Montreal reporter Elmer Ferguson asked what the closed-door discussions had yielded, Kennedy delivered the unvarnished truth: "It's like our old league except that we haven't invited Eddie Livingstone to be part of it."

Two franchises, player raids and wartime strain

Livingstone, a former Ontario Hockey Association referee and journalist for the Toronto Mail and Empire, entered professional ownership by purchasing the Toronto Ontarios in 1914, renaming them the Toronto Shamrocks. Ahead of the 1915–16 season, he bought the Toronto Blueshirts from Frank Robinson for CA$2,000. The league demanded he divest the Shamrocks by November 20, 1915, to avoid owning two franchises. Before a deal could materialise, Frank and Lester Patrick of the Pacific Coast Hockey Association raided the Blueshirts' roster, luring away key skaters including Frank Foyston, Cully Wilson, and goaltender Hap Holmes. To field a team, Livingstone transferred Shamrocks players into Blueshirts sweaters, leaving the Shamrocks assetless; when the deadline passed without a sale, the NHA seized the Shamrocks franchise.

Tensions erupted on multiple fronts. On February 3, 1915, Lichtenhein's Wanderers were awarded a forfeit win when Livingstone refused to ice a team while defencemen George and Howard McNamara attended their dying father's bedside. Lichtenhein offered $3,000 for Livingstone to walk away from hockey; Livingstone countered with an offer of $5,000 for Lichtenhein to shutter the Wanderers. During the 1916–17 campaign, as Canadian military commitments for the First World War stripped rosters, Livingstone sparred over player rights, suspending star Cy Denneny before selling him to Ottawa for an unprecedented $1,800.

Matters reached a boiling point in February 1917 when the 228th (Northern Fusiliers) Battalion of the Canadian Expeditionary Force, which had iced an NHA team, was mobilised overseas. To balance the remaining schedule, rival owners met without Livingstone on February 11, voted to suspend the Blueshirts, and distributed Toronto's players to other clubs via a lottery.

The constitutional dead end at the Windsor Hotel

When the 1916–17 season concluded, the NHA reinstated the Toronto franchise on the condition that Livingstone sell within 60 days. Livingstone refused multiple purchase offers, launched lawsuits against his fellow owners, and secured a court injunction blocking any forced transfer. Rival owners discovered that the NHA constitution contained no mechanism permitting a majority to expel a member club.

Faced with a litigious partner they could neither discipline nor remove, Gorman, Kennedy, Lichtenhein, and Quinn chose to dissolve the operational machinery around him. Gorman remarked that Livingstone was "always arguing" and declared that without him, owners could focus on commercial stability. By suspending the NHA indefinitely and creating the National Hockey League as an entirely separate corporate entity, they left Livingstone holding an empty charter in an inactive league.

A temporary Toronto club lifts the Stanley Cup

Because Quebec faced acute financial difficulties and suspended operations, the new league faced an unbalanced three-team schedule between the Canadiens, Wanderers, and Senators. To secure access to Toronto's Arena Gardens—Canada's modern artificial-ice venue—the NHL granted a temporary franchise to the building's operating company, the Toronto Arena Company. The Arena Company leased Livingstone's former Blueshirts players without his consent.

The NHL opened its inaugural season on December 19, 1917. That temporary Toronto squad, competing without an official nickname, captured the NHL championship and went on to defeat the PCHA's Vancouver Millionaires in March 1918 to claim the Stanley Cup. The Arena Company received a permanent franchise the following season, establishing the lineage of the modern Toronto Maple Leafs. Livingstone spent more than a decade in Canadian courts fighting the seizure of his roster, eventually winning substantial damages from the Arena Company and the defunct NHA, but he never returned to the league born from his exclusion.

item.title: Oliver Bearman Signs Haas Contract Extension for 2027 Season
item.description: The 21-year-old Briton completes the 22-car Formula 1 grid ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix after weeks of contract delays.
item.content:encoded:
Oliver Bearman will remain with Haas for the 2027 Formula 1 season after signing a contract extension ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix at the Lusail International Circuit on Thursday, November 26, 2026. The agreement fills the 22nd and final vacant seat on the 2027 grid across Formula 1's 11 constructors, pairing the 21-year-old British racer with Brazilian rookie Rafael Câmara.

The confirmation resolved weeks of paddock debate, coming four days after Bearman admitted at the Las Vegas Grand Prix that he was "quite disappointed" to reach round 20 of the 2026 championship without signed paperwork. Bearman has served as Haas' primary points scorer this season, collecting 23 of the American outfit's 31 championship points to help the team hold seventh place in the Constructors' Championship ahead of Audi.

Outperforming expectations and anchoring Haas

Bearman secured his full-time Haas seat for the 2025 campaign after making three substitute Grand Prix appearances in 2024. He debuted at age 18 for Ferrari at the 2024 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix as an emergency replacement for Carlos Sainz, followed by two relief drives for Haas in Baku and São Paulo. During his first full season in 2025, Bearman finished fourth at the Mexico City Grand Prix, matching the best race result in Haas team history.

Across 48 career Formula 1 starts leading into the Qatar weekend, Bearman has recorded 71 points. Following an intra-team shakeup that saw Haas part ways with Esteban Ocon earlier in 2026, the British driver emerged as the team's operational leader.

"Continuing with Ollie into 2027 was a natural decision for us," Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said in Thursday's announcement. "We've seen his growth, his commitment, and the quality he brings to the team, both on and off the track. He has a tremendous work ethic and a strong desire to develop both himself and the team, and there is no better person, in my opinion, to lead this team forward."

The Ferrari link and the 2027 grid

Bearman's contract required alignment between Haas and Ferrari, whose Driver Academy the Briton joined in 2021. Ferrari supplies Haas with power units and technical support, and incoming teammate Câmara also emerged from the Scuderia's junior pipeline. With Charles Leclerc under a long-term agreement and Lewis Hamilton contracted through 2027 at Maranello, the Haas extension gives Bearman stability while maintaining his link to Ferrari's future plans.

"This team has played an integral role in my development, and I've felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here," Bearman said. "We've got big ambitions to keep pushing forward, and I'm excited to lead that work, building on what we've achieved, and striving for even more together – we have unfinished business."

Haas' confirmation concludes all driver market movements for 2027, locking in all 22 race seats before the final two rounds of 2026 in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

item.title: Jannik Sinner Withdrawn From 2027 Australian Open Following Right Knee Surgery
item.description: Tennis Australia confirms the two-time Melbourne champion will skip January's Grand Slam tournament to continue his recovery.
item.content:encoded:
Two-time champion Jannik Sinner will miss the 2027 Australian Open while recovering from right knee surgery, tournament organisers confirmed on Thursday, 26 November 2026. The 25-year-old Italian, currently ranked world No. 2, had already shut down his 2026 campaign in October to treat inflammation before undergoing a procedure earlier this week.

Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo confirmed Sinner’s withdrawal from the opening Grand Slam tournament of the season, which begins on 17 January 2027 at Melbourne Park.

"We've been in regular touch with Jannik's team and they've confirmed he won't be joining us for the AO in January following his recent surgery," Abdo said in an official statement to The Associated Press. "Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for AO 2028. We wish him all the very best with his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on court soon."

Surgery Follows Prolonged Tour Absence

Sinner announced on Tuesday, 24 November, that he had undergone what he termed a "minor" operation on his right knee after it failed to heal through non-surgical treatments. The Italian has not competed on the ATP Tour since July 2026, when he defended his Wimbledon crown to claim his fifth career Grand Slam singles championship.

His management confirmed in October that Sinner would sit out the remainder of the 2026 schedule. The current layoff marks his second extended absence from tour competition in two seasons, following an agreed three-month suspension in 2025 settled with the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA).

"I have to respect the protocols at the moment because if we rush things we could have more serious problems," Sinner stated during a news conference in Milan earlier in November. The prolonged hiatus cost him the world No. 1 ranking, which passed to Germany’s Alexander Zverev.

Melbourne Park Record and Australian Impact

Melbourne Park has provided the venue for many of Sinner’s career highlights. In 2024, he won his first Grand Slam title by beating Daniil Medvedev in five sets in the final. He retained the trophy in 2025 with victory over Zverev in the final, before losing in the 2026 semi-finals to Novak Djokovic.

Across seven visits to the Australian Open, Sinner has built a 27-5 match record, an 84 percent success rate. Zverev, who has replaced him at the top of the rankings, now heads to Melbourne as world No. 1.

item.title: David Beckham Surprises 39 Youth Players at Singapore Football Clinic
item.description: The former England captain launched Community Chest's Sports for Good initiative alongside local internationals Hassan Sunny and Izairida Shakira.
item.content:encoded:
Former England captain David Beckham made an unannounced appearance at Bedok South Secondary School on Wednesday morning, November 25, 2026, joining 39 young Singaporean footballers for training drills and an eight-a-side match. The 51-year-old former Manchester United and Real Madrid midfielder attended the session to launch Sports for Good: Football Edition, a youth empowerment program created by Community Chest, the philanthropic arm of Singapore’s National Council of Social Service.

The participants, drawn from Bedok South Secondary School and the network of non-profit Tasek Academy and Social Services, arrived expecting a standard training clinic. Beckham, who has served as a global ambassador for Marina Bay Sands since 2013, joined them through the resort's Sands Cares community engagement programme. He was accompanied on the pitch by veteran Singapore men's goalkeeper Hassan Sunny, women's national goalkeeper Izairida Shakira, and players from Sands United, the integrated resort's staff team.

Grassroots Focus and the Girls2WE Initiative

Organizers designed the multi-year program to combine football coaching with adult mentorship for young people from disadvantaged backgrounds. Tasek Academy chairperson Jane Ittogi attended the launch, which spotlighted the organization’s Girls2WE initiative. The project promotes football participation among girls to build resilience, social connection, and personal confidence.

According to Community Chest managing director Jack Lim, more than half of the children supported through the charity’s existing youth initiatives have recorded measurable gains in leadership and teamwork skills. Community Chest currently funds over 300 social service programs reaching roughly 130,000 individuals across Singapore annually.

Drills, Signed Match Balls, and Local Mentors

During the morning session, Beckham participated directly in passing routines, gave tactical pointers, and distributed autographed footballs to the young players. A 14-year-old participant told The Straits Times that players knew a footballer would attend, but had no advance knowledge that Beckham would step onto the turf.

Senior Parliamentary Secretary for Finance and Manpower Shawn Huang, who co-founded Tasek Academy and serves as MP for West Coast–Jurong West GRC, welcomed the visit. "What an honour to start the morning with Sir David Beckham!" Huang wrote in an Instagram post, praising Beckham's willingness to work alongside grassroots boys' and girls' teams.

Beckham's visit aligns with a recurring series of community clinics held across Southeast Asia during his ambassadorship with Las Vegas Sands Corp. For Singapore's grassroots sector, the initiative integrates local sporting figures like Hassan Sunny alongside international stars to support youth mental wellbeing and broaden athletic participation in neighborhood schools.

item.title: Chan Vathanaka: The Kampot Prodigy Who Put Cambodian Football on the Regional Map
item.description: From Kampot to Japan and the Cambodian Premier League scoring record, then two ACL tears: the story of Cambodia's most prolific forward and the comeback he is still writing.
item.content:encoded:
Chan Vathanaka was born on 23 January 1994 in southern Cambodia's coastal province of Kampot. Armed with an incisive left foot, deceptive acceleration and dead-ball precision, he grew into the defining attacker of modern Cambodian football. Widely known across Southeast Asia under the moniker "CV11", Vathanaka transformed from a teenage prospect in Svay Rieng into an international standard-bearer who broke national scoring records and ventured into professional leagues in Japan and Malaysia.

His structured football education began in 2010 when he joined the youth academy of Preah Khan Reach Svay Rieng at age 16. He made his senior league debut during the 2011–12 Cambodian League season, scoring 10 goals in 17 appearances. That breakthrough prompted domestic giants Boeung Ket to secure his signature in June 2012. Vathanaka immediately validated the move by winning the Cambodian League Best Young Player of the Year award in 2012, followed by the Hun Sen Cup Golden Boot in 2013 and his first Cambodian League Player of the Season award in 2014.

The Record-Shattering Boeung Ket Era

The 2015 campaign established Vathanaka as a regional phenomenon. On 11 July 2015, he struck eight goals in a 12–2 rout of Kirivong Sok Sen Chey, establishing the highest single-match tally by a Cambodian-born player in league history and reaching 16 goals in his first eight matches of the season. Three weeks later, on 1 August 2015, he scored all six goals in a 6–0 win against Asia Europe United. In regional competition at the 2015 Mekong Club Championship, Vathanaka netted a hat-trick to defeat Vietnamese champions Becamex Binh Duong 3–2 in the semi-finals, before Boeung Ket finished as runners-up to Thailand's Buriram United. He concluded the tournament as top scorer with five goals and collected the Most Valuable Player award.

Vathanaka finished the 2015 league season with 37 goals, winning the Golden Boot and the league's Most Valuable Player award, ASEAN Football reported.

His scoring rate remained relentless in 2016. In his first start of that league season, Vathanaka struck a hat-trick in under five minutes in a 6–0 win over CMAC FC. On 21 May 2016 against Svay Rieng, Boeung Ket trailed 1–0 before Vathanaka scored in the 85th, 89th and 93rd minutes—the first a left-foot volley from a high cross—to seal a 3–1 win. He topped the league scoring charts for a second straight year with 22 goals, guiding Boeung Ket to the 2016 Cambodian League championship by a single point on the final matchday and capturing both the league Golden Boot and Player of the Season honors.

Pioneering Stints in Japan and Malaysia

Vathanaka's domestic dominance opened rare foreign doors for Cambodian athletes. In January 2017, he signed on loan with J3 League outfit Fujieda MYFC in Japan, taking his customary number 11 shirt. The transition proved demanding; physical and tactical adaptations limited his game time, and he departed without starting a match, making a single late substitute appearance in the J3 League.

He moved south in December 2017, signing with Malaysia Super League side Pahang FA for the 2018 campaign. He made 10 league appearances and scored once before the club released him midway through the season to register Canadian forward Issey Nakajima. Following a brief return to Boeung Ket, where he contributed to another domestic title run, Vathanaka returned to Malaysia on 18 January 2019 by signing a free contract with PKNS FC.

At PKNS, he switched to jersey number 29. His second Malaysian stint proved more productive: he made over 13 league appearances, including a goal against his former club Pahang in April 2019.

International Milestones and Overcoming Adversity

On the international stage, Vathanaka debuted for Cambodia's senior national team on 22 March 2013 in an AFC Challenge Cup qualifier against Turkmenistan. During the 2018 FIFA World Cup qualifiers on 12 March 2015, he entered off the bench against Macau at the Phnom Penh Olympic Stadium to score twice, including a 30-yard free kick, securing a 3–0 first-leg win. In July 2016, he curled home another direct free kick in a friendly against Singapore. At the 2016 AFF Championship, Vathanaka scored both Cambodian goals in a 3–2 group-stage loss to Malaysia, later adding two more goals against Laos at the 2020 AFF Championship.

Off the pitch, Vathanaka established rituals deeply tied to family and culture. After an injury layoff in September 2015, he spent seven hours recording songs in a studio with Cambodian singer Meas Soksophea. In October 2015, he began celebrating his goals by kissing a tattoo on his right arm, inked as a tribute to his parents and family. His profile led to commercial recognition, including an appointment as goodwill ambassador for telecommunications firm SEATEL in January 2016.

Two Knees, Two Comebacks

Injuries have shaped the second half of his career. On 26 January 2022, in a pre-season cup match against Visakha, Vathanaka tore the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in his right knee. A surgical team from Bangkok Hospital's BASEM sports medicine centre flew to Cambodia to reconstruct it, and he did not play competitive football again until 5 March 2023, more than a year later.

He answered with eight league goals in the 2023–24 Cambodian Premier League season as Boeung Ket finished fourth. Then the same blow struck the other leg. On 22 January 2025, in a Hun Sen Cup round-of-16 tie that Boeung Ket won 8–1 against Kompong Cham, he tore the ACL and meniscus in his left knee. He had surgery the next day.

A second year of rehabilitation followed. In January 2026, days before his 32nd birthday, Boeung Ket named him in their squad again, and he was back on the scoresheet from the penalty spot during the club's Hun Sen Cup run, which ended with a share of third place. His league minutes have been carefully managed since: official Cambodian Premier League records show one appearance, as a substitute, in the 2025–26 season.

The Numbers That Still Stand

No knee injury can erase what came before. Vathanaka is the all-time top scorer of the Cambodian Premier League with 143 goals. He was its Player of the Season three years in a row (2014, 2015 and 2016) and its top scorer in 2015 and 2016. His best years came between the ages of 20 and 25, when his dribbling down the left and his left foot from dead balls made him one of the most dangerous wide forwards in Southeast Asia.

A Final Chapter Still Being Written

At 32, still wearing Boeung Ket's number 11, Vathanaka is no longer the explosive young forward who tore through defences in 2015. The question for Cambodian football is not whether he can repeat a 37-goal season, but how much of that spark two rebuilt knees still allow, and whether a fit, sharp CV11 can still decide big matches from the left flank.

For a generation of Cambodian fans who grew up watching him run at defenders, he remains the player who showed what Cambodian football could look like at its boldest. Every minute he plays now is a chance to prove that the story of the Kampot prodigy has one more chapter in it.

item.title: Jayson Tatum Pours in 41 Points as Celtics Hold Off Wizards 131-116 to Snap Four-Game Skid
item.description: Boston built a 31-point halftime lead behind a 46-point second quarter before weathering Washington's late rally to remain unbeaten in NBA Cup play.
item.content:encoded:
WASHINGTON — Jayson Tatum scored 41 points, grabbed six rebounds and dished eight assists on Tuesday night to guide the Boston Celtics to a 131-116 victory over the Washington Wizards at Capital One Arena, snapping Boston's four-game losing streak.

The result marked Boston's 12th consecutive victory over Washington, lifting the Celtics to 12-6 on the season and a 3-0 record in NBA Cup Eastern Group C.

First-half barrage builds 31-point cushion

Boston seized control during the opening quarter behind center Neemias Queta, who scored 13 of his season-high 21 points before Washington center Anthony Davis made a field goal, sending Boston into the second period with a 34-28 advantage.

The Celtics produced 46 points in the second quarter, hitting 10 three-pointers. Tatum scored 28 points in the first half alone on 9-of-13 shooting from the field and 6-of-9 from deep, highlighted by three straight triples in a span of 1:43 to finish an 11-0 burst that made it 70-38. Paul George added 13 of his 28 points in the second period, guiding Boston to an 80-49 halftime lead.

Wizards surge before Scheierman and Tatum close the door

Washington countered with a 40-24 third quarter, spearheaded by Davis, who finished with 33 points and 13 rebounds. Kyshawn George contributed 24 points, rookie AJ Dybantsa recorded 20 points, 11 rebounds and seven assists, and Trae Young delivered 17 points and 12 assists.

A driving bank shot from Dybantsa with 3:19 remaining capped a 29-point comeback effort to bring Washington within 117-112. Tatum responded on the following possession with a layup, before Baylor Scheierman drilled a corner three-pointer for his first points of the night. Scheierman subsequently added two free throws and another three-pointer, anchoring a closing 14-4 run that halted Washington's three-game winning streak.

"In the second half, I left a lot on the table that I'm going to be mad about tonight," Tatum told NBC Sports Boston. "No lead is safe, and they get paid to play basketball too... So we just tried to weather the storm and answer."

Cup stakes and Friday group decider

The defeat mathematically eliminated Washington (7-12, 2-2 Cup play) from the tournament. Tatum finished shooting 13-of-25 from the floor and 6-of-15 from long range over 37 minutes. Boston returns home to TD Garden on Friday night to face the Atlanta Hawks, where the winner will claim top spot in Eastern Group C and advance to the quarterfinals.

item.title: Arthur Rinderknech Denies ITIA Anti-Doping Charge Over Alleged Test Refusal
item.description: The French world No. 57 rejects the allegations on social media and heads to an independent tribunal without a provisional ban.
item.content:encoded:
French tennis player Arthur Rinderknech was formally charged by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, for allegedly refusing to submit to an anti-doping control. The 31-year-old world No. 57 responded on social media, issuing a complete denial and confirming that he will contest the accusation before an independent panel.

Denial and Independent Tribunal Process

In a statement published on his Instagram account, Rinderknech expressed frustration that an inquiry meant to stay confidential had reached the media. He confirmed that he has formally contested the ITIA charge and exercised his right to have the dispute evaluated by an independent tribunal early in 2027.

The Frenchman asserted that he has never used prohibited substances and stated that presenting the full facts before arbitrators will result in his total exoneration. Following Rinderknech's public comments, the ITIA issued a statement confirming the charge. The governing body noted that it attempts to maintain confidentiality during ongoing proceedings and expressed disappointment that details entered the public domain prematurely.

Under tennis anti-doping regulations, an alleged test refusal does not carry a mandatory provisional suspension. Consequently, Rinderknech remains eligible to compete on the ATP Tour while awaiting his hearing.

Severity of Sanctions and the Vondrousova Precedent

Under the World Anti-Doping Code, refusing or evading a sample collection without compelling justification carries the same baseline penalty as an adverse analytical finding: a four-year ban from all sanctioned competition.

The case mirrors that of 2023 Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova. In June 2026, the Czech player was handed a four-year suspension by the ITIA after being found to have refused an anti-doping control. Vondrousova has since lodged an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport in Lausanne, where proceedings remain pending.

On-Court Context and Upcoming Schedule

Rinderknech achieved a career-high singles ranking of world No. 24 and has recorded notable results at the highest levels of the tour. In October 2025, he advanced to the final of the Shanghai Masters, an ATP Masters 1000 tournament, where he faced his cousin Valentin Vacherot.

His best Grand Slam result came at the 2025 US Open in New York, where he progressed to the fourth round of the men's singles draw. He also reached the third round at Wimbledon in both 2025 and 2026. Because no provisional suspension applies to his case, Rinderknech is eligible to enter tournaments at the start of the 2027 season, including the Australian Open preparation swing in January, ahead of his scheduled tribunal date.

item.title: Former Singapore Captain Rosnani Azman Retires from International Football
item.description: The 29-year-old defender steps aside after 58 caps, an overseas career in Japan and Australia, and over a decade of service to Singapore.
item.content:encoded:
Former Singapore women’s national team captain Siti Rosnani Azman announced her retirement from international football on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, concluding more than a decade of senior service to the Lionesses.

The 29-year-old defender accumulated 58 international caps during her tenure, anchoring Singapore’s back line across multiple regional tournaments. She featured at several editions of the Southeast Asian Games, including the 2023 tournament in Cambodia, and competed at the 19th Asian Games held in Hangzhou, China. She wore the armband in a 2-1 win over Laos in May 2023 and was given the permanent captaincy before a friendly against Pakistan that July.

“Representing Singapore has been one of the greatest honours of my football journey,” Rosnani said in a statement released by the Football Association of Singapore. “Wearing the national colours, leading my teammates as captain and sharing so many memorable moments with the team are experiences I will always be grateful for.”

A Trailblazing Overseas Path

Rosnani's international recognition developed alongside a pioneering club career abroad. After earning the inaugural FAS Women’s Premier League Player of the Year award in 2017, she moved to Australia to play for South West Queensland Thunder in the National Premier Leagues Women.

In September 2021, she made history as the first Singaporean female player to sign a professional contract in Japan when she joined WE League club INAC Kobe Leonessa. She later featured for Kibi International University Charme in Japan's Nadeshiko League before returning to Singapore's domestic circuit in 2023.

Her experience in Japan and Australia provided the Lionesses with rare overseas top-flight pedigree during a transitional phase for women's football across Southeast Asia.

Domestic Silverware

Back on the local circuit, Rosnani joined Albirex Niigata Singapore (later rebranded as FC Jurong), helping the side secure the Women’s Premier League championship in 2025. In 2026, she anchored the club’s defense during its inaugural appearance in the Asian Football Confederation’s Women’s Champions League.

Her international chapter is closed, but her club career goes on with FC Jurong.

item.title: Lehecka and Machac Sweep Canada to Send Czechia Into Davis Cup Semi-Finals
item.description: Captain Tomas Berdych guides Czechs to their first Davis Cup final-four appearance in 12 years with a 2-0 quarter-final triumph in Bologna.
item.content:encoded:
Czechia advanced to the Davis Cup semi-finals on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, defeating 2022 champions Canada 2-0 in the Final 8 quarter-finals at the indoor arena in Bologna, Italy. World No. 14 Jiri Lehecka sealed the tie with a 7-6 (4), 6-2 victory over Felix Auger-Aliassime after Tomas Machac opened proceedings by defeating Liam Draxl in three sets. The result ended a 12-year wait for Czechia, who had not reached the last four of the international men's team tournament since 2014.

Lehecka denies Auger-Aliassime on critical points

Auger-Aliassime, ranked 17th in the world, entered the match having won three of their previous four ATP encounters, including an indoor meeting in Dubai earlier this season. In Tuesday's decisive second rubber, the Canadian generated nine break points in the opening set, including a set point at 5-4, but Lehecka repelled every threat. The 25-year-old Czech forced a tiebreak, firing an ace to secure set point at 6-4 before closing out the 68-minute opener.

"It was a super tough match," Lehecka said in his on-court interview. "I was forced to play very well facing some break points and some tough situations. Felix is such a dangerous player in these conditions, so I'm very proud with the way I converted the chances I had."

Early breaks and Berdych's selection pay off

Lehecka maintained his momentum early in the second set, earning an immediate break of serve to establish a 3-0 lead. At 5-2, Auger-Aliassime saved a match point with a backhand winner, but Lehecka converted his second chance when the Canadian steered a backhand wide to conclude the contest in two hours. "It was a gruelling first set," Auger-Aliassime said. "Maybe there was just a bit of a dip on my end at the start of the second. I tried to fight back, but he was pretty locked in."

Czech captain Tomas Berdych, who won consecutive Davis Cup titles as a player in 2012 and 2013, had surprised observers by selecting world No. 59 Machac over top-20 compatriot Jakub Mensik for the opening singles match. Machac validated the gamble, overcoming 154th-ranked Draxl 6-2, 3-6, 6-2 in one hour and 55 minutes. Machac stormed to a 4-0 lead in the first set and broke Draxl for a 4-2 lead in the decider to hand Czechia early control.

Semi-final awaits against Italy or South Korea

Canada contested the tie without injured singles stars Denis Shapovalov and Gabriel Diallo, leaving Frank Dancevic's side unable to take the tie into a deciding doubles match.

Czechia now move on to Friday's semi-final in Bologna, where they will face the winner of Wednesday's quarter-final clash between defending champions Italy and South Korea. The South Korean team enters Wednesday seeking to reach a historic first Davis Cup semi-final.
